title: Hierarchical slab coalescer and prefill-aware scheduler for variable-length requests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce aggregate padding and improve kernel utilization for mixed-length inference traffic by introducing a hierarchical slab coalescer (slab -> bucket -> microbatch) that is prefill-aware and exposes knobs for kernel selection and decode scheduling. Motivation: current coalescing groups by coarse seqlen buckets which leaves fragmentation when workload has many long-tail sequences. This increases per-token cost and reduces throughput on GPUs with kernel alignment constraints. The new approach should preserve p50/p95 latency SLOs while lowering token-level compute by coalescing into kernel-friendly slabs and prioritizing prefill requests for attention-kv reuse.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end e2e benchmark shows >=20% median padding reduction compared to baseline bucketing on mixed-length synthetic trace; 2) Throughput on resnet50-sized model (baseline model fixture) improves >=1.25x under mixed-length traffic without increasing p95 latency beyond 10% of baseline; 3) No regression in correctness for streaming/partial-prefill workloads (unit tests + integration tests pass); 4) Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rollout can be toggled per-customer; 5) CI artifacts include microbench harness and perf dashboard link.
implementation_notes: Design: 3-tier grouping: 1) Slabs: align to kernel-friendly token widths (e.g., multiples of 16/32 depending on architecture) and prefer GPU memory page alignment to reduce kernel branching; 2) Buckets: within a slab, cluster by prefill vs decode and expected kv reuse; 3) Microbatch: build microbatches respecting SLO budgets (latency-first for low-SLA customers, throughput-first otherwise). Prefill-aware scheduling: track last-kv-hits per client and prioritize prefill requests that can reuse KV cache across subsequent decodes. Kernel selection: annotate slabs with candidate kernels (fused attention for short sequences, flash-attn-v2 for medium, fallback to generic kernel for long sequences) and query kernel profiler at runtime for cost estimates. Config: slab sizes, alignment, and scheduling policy exposed through runtime config and per-customer overrides. Instrumentation: per-slabs metrics (pad tokens saved, kernel choice ratio, microbatch occupancy) and end-to-end traces.
benchmarks: Baseline: current bucketing A on mixed-length trace: mean padding ratio 0.42, throughput 1000 seq/s, p95 lat 120ms. Preliminary lab run (prototype v0.3, A100s): hierarchical slab coalescer -> mean padding ratio 0.30 (28% reduction), throughput 1350 seq/s (+35%), p95 lat 125ms (+4%). In prefill-heavy scenario (40% prefill requests) saw pad reduction 34% and end-to-end tokens/sec +1.4x. Note: microbench used model_fixtures/bert_small.v2 and synthetic trace derived from customer anonymized histograms (contrib/trace-gen). Full perf matrix uploaded to internal dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/ENG-22134 (read-only link).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased scheduling complexity could raise tail latency under bursts. Mitigation: implement conservative SLO-aware admission control and a fast-path that falls back to current bucketing when queue depth spikes. Risk: Kernel selection mispredictions leading to poorer throughput. Mitigation: realtime kernel profiler + lightweight estimator to re-evaluate choices and update slab annotations. Risk: Changes interact with KV cache lifecycle causing cache churn. Mitigation: prefill-aware placement and experimental flag to disable KV-sharing for customers with strict isolation requirements.

Lina (PM) 2025-03-02: Customer impact looks medium; ensure rollout can be reverted per-customer and include cost/latency comparisons in release notes.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime feature flag; 2) Canary on internal dev pool (1% traffic) for 48h; 3) Expand to dedicated test tenants (5-10%) and run cost/regression checks; 4) Open beta for selected enterprise customers with opt-out; 5) Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks with automatic fallback on pad/slo regressions. Rollback: flip feature flag to fall back to legacy bucketing; monitor pad and latency metrics.
qa_criteria: Unit tests for slab alignment + kernel annotation, integration tests for prefill-integration and KV reuse, e2e perf reproducible on lab harness, no p95 > baseline*1.10 during canary. QA owner: Mei Chen.
estimated_savings: Conservative estimate: 18-25% token-level compute reduction for mixed-length workloads. Optimistic lab runs: 30-40% pad reduction and 1.3-1.5x throughput uplift depending on trace shape.
final_notes: This ticket is intended to be incremental: start with conservative slab sizes and an opt-in policy. If successful, we will follow up with per-model quantized kernel profiles and tighter KV-sharing heuristics in a follow-up ticket.
